job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

response.passage: In the bustling town of Kodaikanal, local strawberry farmers are facing a unique challenge this season. Mr. Arjun, the head of the Hillside Cooperative, reported that the farm at Green Valley produced 450 kilograms of strawberries this June. Meanwhile, the smaller plot at Misty Ridge yielded only 280 kilograms. The difference in output is primarily due to the installation of a new automated drip irrigation system at Green Valley, which ensures consistent water supply to the roots. While Misty Ridge relies on traditional rainfall, the efficiency of the new system allows the Green Valley plants to grow faster and produce more fruit. Local shopkeeper Mrs. Meena noted that because the Green Valley harvest is larger, the market price for their berries has dropped to 120 rupees per kilogram to encourage quick sales. In contrast, the rarer Misty Ridge berries are being sold at 180 rupees per kilogram. Residents are now debating whether the technology is worth the investment, as the cost of maintaining the irrigation system is quite high. Despite the debate, the cooperative plans to expand the system to all farms by next year to increase the total regional yield.
response.summary: Kodaikanal strawberry farmers are comparing yields between two farms using different irrigation methods. The farm with the new automated system produced more fruit, leading to lower market prices compared to the traditional farm.
